messages:
tess: Brainstorm: "local watchdog" for canary/A-B that avoids a central rollback choke-point. Requirements: fast local fail, avoid node flapping, tenant isolation, auditable events, and a way for central guardrails to step in if needed. Ideas?

arjun: Love it. Minimal sketch: two-tier fallback + damping. Tier1 = soft-degrade (e.g., route to a quantized/faster model or reduce max tokens). Tier2 = hard-fallback to last-known-good variant. Decision made at edge on a timer, using a dampened signal so single spikes don't flip things.

mike: Key primitives I'd add:
- lease token per-node (short, e.g., 20s) so flips are bound in time
- token-bucket dampener per-tenant to rate-limit how often a tenant can cause flips on that node
- lightweight quorum stamp: nodes gossip a one-line stamp to central telemetry (not for decisioning) so we can quickly detect wide disagreements

arjun: On signals: prefer aggregate-sampled signals rather than pure p99 on production traffic. Example inputs: synthetic probe failures, sampled production errors (per-tenant), and worker-side backpressure (queue depth). Weighting configurable per-workload.

tess: How do we avoid split-brain where half the fleet degrades and half stays?

mike: Accept small transient divergence. Mitigations:
- require majority of requests for that tenant on the node to observe the issue before node flips tenant traffic (avoid single-request flips)
- add conservative recovery rule: require M consecutive healthy ticks OR a central reconcile signal to fully restore traffic

arjun: Also propose a probabilistic reconciliation ping: when nodes disagree stably, they emit a reconciliation event and central watchdog can optionally push a short-lived override key. Central is only for escalation, not routine decisioning.

ops-bot: [note] reconciliation-mode enabled in cluster us-east-2 for canary run at 2026-02-15T11:22:34Z

tess: Policy example (compact):
```
policy_version: "edge-watchdog-v1"
scopes: [tenant, node]
input_signals:
  - synthetic_fail_pct(weight=0.5, window_s=30)
  - sampled_error_rate(weight=0.3, window_s=60)
  - queue_backlog(weight=0.2, window_s=15)
thresholds:
  soft_degrade: 0.6
  hard_fallback: 0.9
damping:
  lease_s: 20
  bucket_capacity: 3
  refill_s: 60
recovery:
  healthy_ticks_required: 4
  central_reconcile_allowed: true
telemetry:
  emit_stamp: true
  trace_header: x-edge-watchdog: inst_id,reason,policy_rev
```

mike: Operational notes:
- Keep decision off the hot path; evaluate on a fixed tick.
- Store overrides in ephemeral memory with clear TTLs.
- Make soft-degrade reversible faster than hard-fallback (shorter TTL).
- Enforce tenant caps so a noisy tenant can't flip node-global behavior.

arjun: Security/compat: support operator force via named key (e.g., control-plane.force.edge_watchdog.v1) and require audit log entry. For Private/Dedicated, allow control-plane-sourced policy but require same schema.

tess: Observability: emit metrics edge_watchdog_override_total{scope,reason,tenant,inst} and a sampled event stream with the stamp so SRE can correlate. Also surface a small dashboard showing per-tenant flip-rate and average duration.

mike: Fail-safes: if a node loses probe connectivity or telemetry channel, default to conservative mode (prefer soft-degrade) not hard-fallback. Also add a circuit-breaker that prevents more than K hard-fallbacks per node per hour.

ops-bot: [deploy-check] policy schema edge-watchdog-v1 lint OK. 1 info: consider exposing "max_hard_fallbacks_per_hour".

tess: Action list: 1) arjun to prototype the tick loop + token-bucket damping (PR). 2) mike to draft telemetry stamp format + dashboard mock. 3) infra to document signals we own vs runtime signals and recommend default weights. 4) ops to define central reconcile runbook (when to escalate). Target: small canary trial next week.

arjun: Quick perf note: keep evaluator O(1) per tick per tenant on a node; avoid per-request aggregation. Use approximate counters for sampled metrics.

mike: Sounds good. Also keep schema forward-compatible (allow new signals and weights).

tess: Great sync. We'll iterate on numbers during the trial. Thanks folks :raised_hands:
